recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the older Condition.evidence short/definition unless Patient Care reopens the post-FHIR-42981 scope; any generated diagram staleness should be handled separately from this FHIR-11026 reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-11026 asked to clarify the relationship between Condition and Observation for absence/refutation scenarios. Its Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution updated the Assertions of Condition Absence guidance, clarified the refuted verification status definition, and changed Condition.evidence wording to support verification status including evidence that confirmed or refuted the condition.
initial_application: Commit f403e6bf3448762019dc45c82cfbb2aaa9362585 explicitly applied FHIR-11026/J#11026 to source/condition/condition-notes.xml and the then-authoritative Condition spreadsheet. Subsequent source restructuring preserved the narrative guidance, the refuted code definition moved to THO with terminology duplicate removal, and Condition.evidence kept the verification-status wording until a later Patient Care decision changed it.
additional_context: Condition and Observation are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Related issues already on the combined branch cover the same family: FHIR-11077 for the original absence section, FHIR-15610 for the older Condition.evidence wording, FHIR-28458 for later refuted-status guidance, and FHIR-42981 for the later intentional broadening of Condition.evidence beyond verification status. Direct FHIR-11026 Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community decision.
reconciliation: An empty no-change audit commit was published. The current Condition notes already convey the refuted Condition guidance and the use of Condition.verificationStatus and Condition.evidence; the current Condition.evidence element should remain broader because FHIR-42981 superseded the older verification-status-only wording; and the current THO condition-ver-status code system still has the FHIR-11026 refuted definition.
